title: Share ownership and transfer restrictions
summary: Establish who owns the sale shares, reconcile the ownership evidence, and identify the consents, waivers and completion steps required to transfer them.

transaction_context.materiality_basis: The ability to transfer the agreed sale shares is fundamental. Distinguish missing evidence from conflicting title and assess the effect of each restriction on the agreed completion timetable.

facts.statement: Compare the current register with the cap table and SPA sale schedule: each registered holder, share class and number. Companies House filings and PSC information are cross-checks, not substitutes for the register. Check any historic central-register election where relevant.

Check certificates and relevant historic transfers or transmission evidence. A missing certificate is an evidence gap, not proof of invalid ownership. For uncertificated holdings, check the applicable system evidence. Allotment validity is assessed separately.

Select all that apply after checking beneficial ownership, trusts, nominee arrangements, grants of representation, powers of attorney, charges and adverse claims. Record actual arrangements even if the required documents are already ready.

Select all that apply to this transaction. Review the current articles, shareholder agreement and amendments, including board discretion to refuse registration. Check who can waive each right and the notice periods. Do not assume statutory allotment pre-emption applies to transfers.

Check written consents and waivers, notice periods, signatory authority, releases and the certificate package against the proposed timetable. Ready means all necessary evidence and steps are effective or documented for delivery at completion; an agreement in principle is not enough.

key_questions.question: Does the register of members agree with the sellers and shares in the sale schedule?
key_questions.purpose: Compare the current register with the cap table and SPA sale schedule: each registered holder, share class and number. Companies House filings and PSC information are cross-checks, not substitutes for the register. Check any historic central-register election where relevant.

answer_options.clear: Yes — holders, classes and numbers reconcile
answer_options.incomplete: Partly — records are incomplete or out of date

key_questions.question: Do the certificates and supporting ownership documents agree with those records?
key_questions.purpose: Check certificates and relevant historic transfers or transmission evidence. A missing certificate is an evidence gap, not proof of invalid ownership. For uncertificated holdings, check the applicable system evidence. Allotment validity is assessed separately.

answer_options.clear: Yes — certificates or applicable ownership evidence reconcile
answer_options.certificate: Only share certificates are missing — other title evidence agrees
answer_options.gaps: Other supporting ownership evidence is missing or incomplete
answer_options.both: Share certificates and other supporting evidence are missing
answer_options.conflict: No — supporting documents conflict with the ownership records

key_questions.question: Are there beneficial interests, signing arrangements or claims over the sale shares?
key_questions.purpose: Select all that apply after checking beneficial ownership, trusts, nominee arrangements, grants of representation, powers of attorney, charges and adverse claims. Record actual arrangements even if the required documents are already ready.

answer_options.none: None — sellers own legally and beneficially, with no identified claims or security
answer_options.nominee: Nominee, trust or separate beneficial owner
answer_options.representative: Personal representative, attorney or other authorised signatory
answer_options.security: Charge, pledge or other security over the sale shares
answer_options.claim: Adverse ownership claim or disputed authority

key_questions.question: Which transfer requirements are engaged under the articles or shareholder agreement?
key_questions.purpose: Select all that apply to this transaction. Review the current articles, shareholder agreement and amendments, including board discretion to refuse registration. Check who can waive each right and the notice periods. Do not assume statutory allotment pre-emption applies to transfers.

answer_options.none: None — documents reviewed and no transfer restriction is engaged
answer_options.board: Board approval or discretion to refuse registration
answer_options.other: Lock-in, permitted-transfer condition or deed of adherence
answer_options.unknown: Not yet checked — documents or their effect are unclear

key_questions.question: Are the required ownership and transfer steps ready for completion?
key_questions.purpose: Check written consents and waivers, notice periods, signatory authority, releases and the certificate package against the proposed timetable. Ready means all necessary evidence and steps are effective or documented for delivery at completion; an agreement in principle is not enough.

answer_options.ready: Ready — all required evidence and steps are effective or documented for completion
answer_options.pending: Pending — documents, notices or approvals remain outstanding
answer_options.blocked: Blocked — a required step is refused, disputed or cannot be completed in time

risk_assessment.rationale: An unassessed position starts at 2/5. Isolated missing certificates with otherwise consistent evidence remain low risk; other gaps or unconfirmed transfer steps are medium risk, ownership conflicts high risk, and adverse claims or blocked completion steps very high risk. Readiness never overrides conflicting evidence.

risk_factors.description: Ownership records or supporting documents conflict.
Certificates are missing; assess the other evidence without presuming invalid ownership.
A required title or transfer step cannot be completed on the proposed timetable.

recommended_actions.recommendation: Reconcile the register, supporting title documents and SPA sale schedule; review the current articles and shareholder agreement for the proposed transfer.
recommended_actions.rationale: Selected and prioritised by the answer-driven rules for the chosen transaction side.

recommended_actions.recommendation: Agree the SPA certificate deliverables and a proportionate lost-certificate indemnity or replacement procedure under the articles. Verify the other title evidence; this package does not resolve conflicting ownership records.
recommended_actions.rationale: Selected and prioritised by the answer-driven rules for the chosen transaction side.

recommended_actions.recommendation: Require evidence-based title resolution before completion, with corrective documents or specialist advice on register rectification where needed. A replacement certificate or warranty alone does not resolve a title dispute.
recommended_actions.rationale: Selected and prioritised by the answer-driven rules for the chosen transaction side.

recommended_actions.recommendation: Identify the transferor, beneficial owner and authorised signatory in the SPA. Deliver any trustee or nominee authority, beneficiary consent or release, grant of representation or power of attorney actually required.
recommended_actions.rationale: Selected and prioritised by the answer-driven rules for the chosen transaction side.

recommended_actions.recommendation: Require release of each charge or pledge over the sale shares against any agreed payment, with binding release documents and a coordinated funds flow as SPA completion deliverables.
recommended_actions.rationale: Selected and prioritised by the answer-driven rules for the chosen transaction side.

recommended_actions.recommendation: Schedule the required board, shareholder and investor steps in the SPA, with a covenant to obtain effective written approvals or waivers from the correct right holders and comply with transfer notices and deadlines.
recommended_actions.rationale: Selected and prioritised by the answer-driven rules for the chosen transaction side.

recommended_actions.recommendation: Reflect any engaged tag, drag, lock-in or adherence terms in the SPA: eligible holders, thresholds, notices, timing and execution. Do not assume a drag binds every holder or that the shareholder agreement terminates automatically.
recommended_actions.rationale: Selected and prioritised by the answer-driven rules for the chosen transaction side.

recommended_actions.recommendation: Obtain seller-specific SPA warranties covering ownership, authority to sell, freedom from encumbrances and absence of undisclosed transfer restrictions. Address legal and beneficial title expressly where they differ.
recommended_actions.rationale: Selected and prioritised by the answer-driven rules for the chosen transaction side.

recommended_actions.recommendation: Identify certificate gaps, title discrepancies, beneficial interests and transfer requirements against the relevant SPA warranties. Describe the evidence and agreed solution; disclosure alone does not cure title or release transfer rights.
recommended_actions.rationale: Selected and prioritised by the answer-driven rules for the chosen transaction side.

recommended_actions.recommendation: Specify executed transfers, certificates or agreed loss evidence, board registration steps and applicable Stamp Duty formalities in the SPA completion schedule. Address interim voting and dividends pending registration where lawful.
recommended_actions.rationale: Selected and prioritised by the answer-driven rules for the chosen transaction side.

recommended_actions.recommendation: Make material unresolved title, release or transfer steps objective SPA conditions or completion deliverables, with a covenant to progress them, an agreed longstop and a defined termination route.
recommended_actions.rationale: Selected and prioritised by the answer-driven rules for the chosen transaction side.

recommended_actions.recommendation: For an identified title conflict or adverse claim, negotiate a specific SPA indemnity with defined losses, claim conduct, limits and no double recovery; consider security if recovery is doubtful. It is not a substitute for the ability to transfer title.
recommended_actions.rationale: Selected and prioritised by the answer-driven rules for the chosen transaction side.

then.explanation: Establish the missing evidence or reconcile the recorded conflict before relying on the sale schedule.
A missing certificate calls for an agreed evidence package, without assuming ownership is invalid.
Conflicting records or an adverse claim require title resolution, beyond certificate replacement.
Document the actual capacity and beneficial interests behind the transfer.
Release security over the sale shares through completion mechanics.
Comply with or obtain effective waivers of the engaged transfer requirements.
Implement the applicable tag, drag, lock-in or adherence route.
Address each seller's title and capacity in the SPA.
Disclose the specific evidence gaps, arrangements and restrictions.
Document the actual transfer and the route to registration.
Protect material unresolved completion dependencies proportionately.
Allocate an identified title exposure without treating an indemnity as a cure.

notes:
Ownership evidence: The register is prima facie evidence, subject to the statutory treatment of historic central-register elections. Certificates are evidence, not conclusive title. A missing document does not by itself invalidate ownership. Ordinary Companies House filings and PSC records do not establish the seller's title.

Beneficial ownership: Identify legal and beneficial interests separately. Trusts are not entered on an England and Wales company's register of members (section 126).

Transfer restrictions: Apply the company's actual articles and shareholder agreement. Model articles apply only if adopted and not displaced. Transfer pre-emption is document-specific; statutory allotment pre-emption is a separate question. Board approval alone does not waive another holder's contractual rights.

Completion: A proper transfer instrument is generally required, subject to statutory exceptions. Registration and applicable Stamp Duty formalities may follow contractual completion; agree any interim rights expressly.

Scope: Defective allotments are outside this issue. Option Holders remains a separate issue.
